The pin is updated here as an explicit, reviewable change, and it still targets the CLEAN detached-worktree blob (HEAD + LIVE hunk), never a dirty worktree blob.P21-R2-A established this baseline (production memory runtime SHA-256). Any OTHER production change to these files must likewise be an explicit update to this file. These three hashes are updated here as an explicit, reviewable change. The signal is LATENT: the orchestrator does not consume it, so user-visible recall semantics are unchanged (24-row semantic delta matrix still 10 CHANGED / 14 SAME). Any OTHER production change to a pinned file must likewise be an explicit update to this file. R2-E1b (P21-R2 Glossary + ColdStart retrieval cutover) activated the glossary and coldStart channels and added the activation-policy seam, so the pinned hashes for the touched production files are updated here as an explicit, reviewable change. memory-retrieval-core.js is NOT among them: the canonical ranking/selection implementation is still byte-identical to the R2-A baseline. Any OTHER production change to a pinned file must likewise be an explicit update to this file. R2-F1a (canonical selector + exploration closure) deliberately modified memory-retrieval-core.js: D-3 full-remaining uniform exploration (the old top-10 prefix window violated MEMORY_RECALL_CONTRACT §9 MUST NOT), D-4 oversized candidates now skip instead of breaking the loop, the memory header is now deducted from maxChars so chars <= maxChars holds, and opts.allowExploration became a real option. The pinned hash is updated accordingly. BEHAVIOURAL evidence for this transition lives in tests/fixtures/memory-recall-r2f-baseline/ (static pre-F frozen data) + tests/test_memory_recall_r2f_delta.js — NOT in this hash file, which only records integrity. R2-F1b (P21-R2 session cooldown: turnIndex propagation into Home Node retrieval + gateway lifecycle wiring + browser session-state/exposure seams) updated the pinned hashes for the touched production files as an explicit, reviewable change; untouched pinned files keep their baseline canonical values. R2-H2 (canonical activation wiring: browser recall routes activation through the memory authority in canonical mode — remote-first, with the mirror SET from the authoritative response; no revision bump, no change_log, no schema change, no migration) updated the pinned hashes for the three touched production files as an explicit, reviewable change. R2-H3 (activation retry/idempotency semantics: AUTO_RETRY=NONE, the endpoint is an explicitly non-idempotent mutation, and transport-level ambiguous outcomes are distinguished from definite failures — mirror never guesses, no schema/migration) updated the pin for the one touched production file as an explicit, reviewable change. R4-A.2 (Activation Authority Repair + Baseline Restoration) modified assets/js/memory.js to close two live mirror-truth bypasses and one latent fallthrough: (1) writeOneLineToMemory no longer bumps activationCount/lastActivated straight into the browser mirror — writing a one-liner is content production, not a recall selection; (2) saveInlineEdit no longer stamps lastActivated=now, which had been inflating the LegacyMemoryValue recency factor on every content edit; (3) recordMemoryActivation's canonical branch is now structurally fail-closed, so a rejecting or throwing authority can never fall through to a local optimistic +1. Home Node activation authority, remote-first ordering, the authoritative SET of mirror telemetry, AUTO_RETRY=NONE, and the revision/change_log semantics are all unchanged, and mirror/off host-local behaviour is preserved. R4-A.3 (Foundation Closure Reconciliation) closed one residual ambiguity in the same file, still without touching the authority contract: recordMemoryActivation now distinguishes NO AUTHORITY (the resolver returned null, so the existing host-local fallback still applies) from AUTHORITY RESOLUTION FAILED (an authority object was resolved but its mode could not be read — a throwing shape read, or no status() at all — which is ambiguous, so it returns 0 and never makes a local canonical guess). It also records the structural proof that _ibMemoryAuthority() itself cannot throw: its whole body sits inside try/catch and returns null. The pin still targets the CLEAN committed blob (HEAD + R4 repair) established on a detached worktree — never a dirty worktree blob. R4-A.4 (Canonical Memory Content Authority audit) then hardened ONE boundary in the same file and left every content write path untouched: recordMemoryActivation now validates the authority mode against the declared vocabulary {canonical, mirror, off}, so an unrecognised, missing, null or unreadable mode fails closed (return 0, mirror untouched) instead of being treated as mirror/off. The audit found NO canonical-content bypass: every browser memory content write (dbPut/dbDelete on the memories store) is routed by home-node-bootstrap's window.dbPut override to memoryAuthority.put/remove, which is remote-first in canonical mode and never writes the mirror on failure. This pin is updated here as an explicit, reviewable change. R4-A.5 (Canonical Content Retry + Authority Downgrade Closure) then touched assets/js/home-node-bootstrap.js — the ONLY file besides memory.js in this whole R4 foundation line — and changed exactly two things inside window.dbPut / window.dbDelete: (1) canonical memory content mutations (put AND delete) no longer go through withRetry, because a retried ambiguous write re-sends the SAME payload and would overwrite a newer concurrent commit (contentFingerprint idempotency is SAME-STATE ONLY, and the ordinary path has no requestId and no CAS — store semantics are LAST-WRITE-WINS); the chat store keeps its existing 3-attempt retry untouched. (2) when MODE is canonical but memoryAuthority could not be assembled, memory writes now FAIL CLOSED with a named error (memory-authority-unavailable) instead of silently writing a second local truth, matching the existing understanding-write-closed / moments-write-closed guards; the legitimate mirror / off local modes are unchanged. No schema, no migration. R4-A.6 (Startup Memory Authority Health Closure) then closed the one window A.5 could not reach: when home-node-bootstrap aborts BEFORE installing the window.dbPut/dbDelete override (missing chat-authority factory, missing window.__ibCoreDb, missing home-node-client remote factory, or a load-time throw), the override simply does not exist, so A.5's in-override guard can never run and memory writes silently fell through to the raw IndexedDB writer. The same file now installs a provisional canonical memory guard at the very top of the IIFE — before any dependency check — which refuses memories put/delete with code memory-authority-not-ready whenever canonical is intended and the protocol is not file:, while forwarding every other store verbatim and leaving MODE=mirror / MODE=off / file:// host-local semantics untouched. The real bootstrap replaces the guard by direct assignment (never wrapping it), the install is idempotent, and each of the three early exits now emits memory-bootstrap-dependency-missing plus a degraded IB.homeNode memory surface reusing the existing status() shape. Still no schema, no migration. P21-R4-LIVE-2.1 (Vault-Authorized Runtime Interpretation Boundary) touched assets/js/home-node-bootstrap.js — the ONLY pinned file it changed — by adding one narrow, explicitly-invoked surface (IB.homeNode.runtime: instance / available / the single verb runMemoryInterpretation) that delegates to the new browser transport in assets/js/home-node-client.js. It adds no timer, no per-turn hook and no automatic invocation, so the recall authority/mirror/fallback semantics, the window.dbPut / window.dbDelete guards and the early-exit degraded surfaces are byte-for-byte unchanged; the memory recall contract, the activation authority and every pinned behaviour are unaffected. Its hash is updated here as an explicit, reviewable change. The pins for assets/js/memory.js and assets/js/communication.js are deliberately NOT updated: those two files carry uncommitted user work in this worktree, and this file must never pin a dirty worktree blob (see R4-LIVE-1's note), so their P18 mismatch is a pre-existing property of this worktree, not a transition of this phase. P21-R4-LIVE-3.2 (Desktop Recall Selection Authority Cutover Foundation) then touched services/home-node/memory-retrieval.js with a COMMENT-ONLY correction: the P21-R2-C-era comment claimed the host deliberately omits `turn` from buildOpts so that 「active behavior is always legacy」, while the same function has set `turn: {message, conversationId, isFirstTurn, conversationSignalAvailable}` since R2-D — the comment described the wiring stage, not the shipped semantics, and would have led a reader to believe this host still runs the legacy path. No executable line changed (the diff is comments only); the pin is updated here as an explicit, reviewable change so the file stays byte-pinned to the clean-worktree blob. This phase does not commit. P21-R4-LIVE-3.3 (Server Recall Boundary Closure) then made two SEAM changes to the same file, both of which default to today's behaviour: (1) `includeHeader` is no longer hard-coded false but an explicit option, `options.includeHeader === true`, so every existing Host call site that passes nothing keeps byte-identical output while the new desktop-parity recall boundary can request the desktop wrapper's selection-budget semantics; (2) the wrapper now forwards the caller's `glossaryProvider` / `getGlossaryEntries` into buildOpts exactly as the desktop wrapper does, closing a wrapper gap in which the server-side glossary channel could never receive a catalog. No glossary algorithm is duplicated: both wrappers feed the orchestrator's single resolveGlossaryCatalog / glossary-catalog factory, and the provider is injected by the server assembly only (never taken from a request). The pin is updated here as an explicit, reviewable change. P21-R4-LIVE-3.3 (Activation Turn Guard) modified services/home-node/memory-store.js by adding ONE optional, additive seam to recordActivation: when options.turnId is present, the same (turnId, memoryId) pair produces at most ONE canonical activation increment per open session, and a repeat is reported honestly (ok:true, updated:0, duplicated:[...], reason:'turn-duplicate') instead of a silent success; when turnId is absent the result shape and behaviour are byte-identical to before, so every legacy caller is unchanged. The guard is IN-MEMORY ONLY (bounded to the most recent 64 turns, cleared on every open()), adds no schema, no migration and no durable idempotency table, and does NOT survive a Home Node restart: a replayed OLD turn after a restart can increment again, which is stated in the code and in this note rather than claimed away. Its canonical hash is updated here as an explicit, reviewable change, and it still targets the clean worktree blob. P21-R4-LIVE-3.3.1 (Server Recall Boundary Exact Closure) then made a COMMENT-ONLY change to services/home-node/memory-store.js: the activation-guard rationale no longer says an unscoped 'exactly-once' and instead states the frozen scope (ACTIVATION_TURN_GUARD = IN_PROCESS_TURN_SCOPED, SAME_PROCESS_SAME_TURN_DUPLICATE = NO_INCREMENT, DIFFERENT_TURN = INCREMENT_ALLOWED, CROSS_PROCESS_RESTART_GUARANTEE = NONE, CROSS_RESTART_EXACTLY_ONCE = NO, ACTIVATION_AUTO_RETRY = NONE). No executable line changed; the hash is updated here as an explicit, reviewable change. P21-R4-LIVE-3.4 (Desktop client recall verb): assets/js/home-node-bootstrap.js gained ONE additive verb on the existing runtime surface (runtime.runMemoryRecall), mirroring runtime.runMemoryInterpretation exactly — same remote instance, same credential path, same shape-stable client-diagnostic envelope when the factory is absent; the closed payload construction lives in assets/js/home-node-client.js. No recall selection, exposure, session, activation, provider or persistence behaviour changes: runMemoryInterpretation and every other verb are byte-identical, and the new verb is never called automatically. The pin is updated here as an explicit, reviewable change. P21-R4-LIVE-3.4 (Server recall authoritative turn lifecycle) modified services/home-node/memory-retrieval.js in two additive ways: (1) the group-chat options are no longer hardcoded — `isGroup` / `groupMemEnabled` now come from `options.isGroup === true` / `options.groupMemEnabled === true`, so the default remains false/false and every existing Host (mobile 1v1) is byte-identical while the desktop group path can be expressed; (2) `reinforce(ids, {turnId})` forwards the caller turn identity to the LIVE-3.3 turn-scoped store guard, while the frozen literal `const res = store.recordActivation(ids, { at: at });` is preserved verbatim for the no-turnId legacy path (both branches call the same store method — there is no second write entry point). Its canonical hash is updated here as an explicit, reviewable change.
